title: Drinking Bacteria and Spinning Plates: Tales of Scientists Who Asked Why
title_zh: 喝下细菌与旋转餐盘：科学家追问“为什么”的故事
intro_zh: 本文实际词数约850词，包含6个CET-4重点词，配有中文翻译与4道阅读理解题。

paragraphs.en: In the history of science, many great discoveries did not begin with a clear goal or practical purpose. They came from simple curiosity—the urge to know why something happens. This inner drive has led scientists to ask questions that others ignored. Almost every field, from astronomy to zoology, has been built by such questioning. This article presents two famous examples from medicine and physics. In both cases, researchers risked their reputations or even their health, simply because they wanted to understand nature. Their stories show that the desire to learn is one of the strongest forces in science.
paragraphs.zh: 在科学史上，许多伟大的发现并非始于明确的目标或实际目的。它们源于简单的好奇心——知道某事为何发生的冲动。这种内在驱动力促使科学家提出他人忽视的问题。从天文学到动物学，几乎每个领域都建立在这些追问之上。本文介绍医学和物理学中的两个著名例子。在这两个案例中，研究人员冒着名誉甚至健康的风险，只因为他们想理解自然。他们的故事表明，学习的欲望是科学中最强大的力量之一。

paragraphs.en: In the early 1980s, doctors believed that stomach ulcers were caused by stress or excess acid. They taught that bacteria could not live in the human stomach because acid kills them. But Australian pathologist Robin Warren noticed small curved bacteria in stomach biopsies from patients with gastritis. No one believed his observation. It was viewed as laboratory contamination. However, Warren thought this phenomenon deserved attention. He met a young physician, Barry Marshall, who shared his curiosity. Together, they began to investigate.
paragraphs.zh: 在20世纪80年代初，医生们认为胃溃疡是由压力或胃酸过多导致的。教科书说细菌不能在人的胃里存活，因为胃酸会杀死它们。但澳大利亚病理学家罗宾·沃伦在胃炎患者的胃活检中注意到小而弯曲的细菌。没有人相信他的观察，认为那是实验室污染。然而，沃伦认为这一现象值得关注。他遇到了年轻医生巴里·马歇尔，后者同样充满好奇。两人便开始一起调查。

paragraphs.en: Marshall and Warren developed a hypothesis that these bacteria caused stomach ulcers. But to prove it, they had to grow the organism in the laboratory, which was extremely difficult. They tried for many months without success. Sometimes the lab staff accidentally threw away cultures that had grown after several days. Finally, after one lucky break, they obtained a pure culture of the spiral bacterium, later named Helicobacter pylori. In 1983, they tried to infect laboratory animals, but the animals did not develop ulcers. Many medical journals rejected their studies, and the scientific community remained doubtful.
paragraphs.zh: 马歇尔和沃伦提出了一个假说：这些细菌导致胃溃疡。但要证明这一点，他们必须在实验室中培养这种微生物，而这极其困难。他们尝试了好几个月都没有成功。有时实验室工作人员不小心把已经生长了几天的培养物扔掉了。经过一次意外的幸运，他们终于获得了一种螺旋状细菌的纯培养，后来命名为“幽门螺杆菌”。1983年，他们尝试感染实验动物，但动物没有发生溃疡。许多医学杂志拒绝发表他们的研究，科学界依旧怀疑。

paragraphs.en: Marshall decided to take a desperate step to prove his idea. He drank a tube of liquid containing the bacteria. Within days, he developed stomach pain, nausea, and vomiting. An endoscopy showed that his stomach was full of bacteria and had active inflammation. He then took antibiotics and recovered completely. This self-experiment offered strong evidence that H. pylori could infect humans and cause disease. It was a classic example of putting one’s life on the line for science. Decades later, his action is remembered as one of the most brave and curious experiments in modern medicine.
paragraphs.zh: 马歇尔决定冒险采取一步来证明自己的想法。他喝下一管含有细菌的培养液。几天后，他开始出现胃疼、恶心和呕吐。内窥镜检查显示他的胃里满是细菌，并有活动性炎症。随后他服用抗生素，完全康复了。这个自我实验提供了强有力的证据：幽门螺杆菌能感染人类并导致疾病。这是一个为科学不惜冒险的经典例子。几十年后，他的行动被视为现代医学中最勇敢和最具好奇心的实验之一。

paragraphs.en: At first, the medical community still doubted the discovery. But further evidence soon appeared. Researchers around the world found that Helicobacter pylori was present in about half of the world’s population, and many infected individuals develop ulcers. Today, it is known that over 80% of gastric ulcers and up to 90% of duodenal ulcers are linked to this bacterium. Marshall and Warren’s work changed the way doctors diagnose and treat ulcers. In 2005, they received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine. Their victory was a triumph of curiosity over common belief.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，医学界仍怀疑这一发现。但更多证据很快出现。世界各地的研究者发现，幽门螺杆菌存在于约一半的世界人口中，许多感染者会发展成溃疡。如今人们知道，超过80%的胃溃疡和高达90%的十二指肠溃疡与这种细菌有关。马歇尔和沃伦的工作改变了医生诊断和治疗溃疡的方式。2005年，他们获得了诺贝尔生理学或医学奖。他们的胜利是好奇心战胜普遍信念的一次胜利。

paragraphs.en: One might think that such stories are rare in physics, but they exist. In 1946, the physicist Richard Feynman was having lunch at a university cafeteria. He noticed a plate flying in the air. The plate had a blue medallion on it, and as it spun, the medallion rotated slightly faster than the wobble. Feynman felt a strong urge to solve this puzzle. He later said that he had no serious purpose, but he could not resist the question. Feynman calculated the relationship between the spin and wobble. He found it was exactly two to one. Then he continued to think about rotating particles, which later connected to quantum electrodynamics.
paragraphs.zh: 有人可能认为这类故事在物理学中很少，但确实存在。1946年，物理学家理查德·费曼在大学食堂吃午饭。他注意到一个旋转的盘子在空中。盘子上有个蓝色的徽章，当它旋转时，徽章转动的速度比晃动略快。费曼有一种强烈的冲动去解开这个谜。他后来说当时没有严肃的目的，但他无法抗拒那个问题。费曼计算了旋转和晃动之间的关系，发现比率正好是二比一。然后他继续思考旋转的粒子，这后来与量子电动力学联系起来。

paragraphs.en: In his Nobel lecture in 1965, Feynman told this story to illustrate the value of curiosity. He explained that he played with the plate just for fun, without expecting any importance. However, this playful research led to useful equations in modern physics. Feynman’s experience encourages scientists to pursue any question that fascinates them, no matter how trivial it seems. The line between serious science and childlike imagination is often thin. Many fundamental laws have come from what appeared to be silly distractions.
paragraphs.zh: 在1965年的诺贝尔演讲中，费曼讲述了这件事来说明好奇心的价值。他解释说自己只是好玩地研究那个盘子，没有期望产生什么重要性。然而，这个游戏般的研究带来了现代物理学中有用的方程式。费曼的经历鼓励科学家去追求任何让他们着迷的问题，无论看起来多么琐碎。严肃科学与孩子般的想象之间的界限往往很薄。许多基本定律都源自那些看似愚蠢的消遣。

paragraphs.en: Both Marshall and Feynman faced controversy at first. Their peers mocked their questions and results. Marshall’s bacterial theory threatened decades of accepted practice. Feynman’s 'playing' was considered unimportant by some. But because they trusted their own eyes and reasoning, they did not give up. Eventually, they not only proved their points but also opened entirely new paths. This reminds us that hypotheses are not just abstract ideas; they are stepping stones that scientists must test with courage.
paragraphs.zh: 马歇尔和费曼最开始都面临争议。同行嘲笑他们的问题和成果。马歇尔的细菌理论威胁了已沿用数十年的权威做法。费曼的“玩耍”被一些人认为不重要。但因为相信自己的观察和推理，他们没有放弃。最终，他们不仅证明了自己的观点，还开辟了全新的道路。这提醒我们，假说不仅仅是抽象的想法，它们是科学家必须用勇气去测试的垫脚石。

paragraphs.en: Curiosity is often the most valuable quality a scientist can have. It drives us to see beyond what others believe and to challenge common knowledge. Marshall’s dangerous drink and Feynman’s spinning plate are only two examples from many fields. Whether studying galaxies or microbes, scientists who ask 'why' are the ones who move civilization forward. So the next time you find yourself curious about something ordinary, remember: that simple wonder might just be the beginning of a great adventure.
paragraphs.zh: 好奇心常常是科学家最宝贵的品质。它驱使我们超越他人的认知，挑战已有的常识。马歇尔危险的自我实验和费曼的旋转餐盘只是众多领域中的两个例子。无论是研究星系还是微生物，那些追问“为什么”的科学家才是推动文明前进的人。所以下一次当你对某件寻常的事物感到好奇时，请记住：那份简单的惊奇可能正是一场伟大冒险的开始。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Scientists should risk their health to prove theories.
Curiosity that drives scientists to ask questions can lead to great discoveries.
Medicine and physics are the most important fields in science.
Scientific discoveries are often rejected by the public.
questions.explain: 文章主要通过马歇尔和费曼两个例子说明好奇心驱动科学家提问并最终带来重大发现，因此B（主旨）正确。A过于片面，C和D均非文章主旨。

questions.q: Why did Barry Marshall drink a liquid containing bacteria?
options: He wanted to test his hypothesis on himself because animal experiments failed.
He wanted to become sick and be treated.
He wanted to win the Nobel Prize.
He believed the bacteria were harmless.
questions.explain: 文中提到动物实验未能让动物得溃疡，马歇尔才决定自我实验（Using himself as a subject），因此A正确。B不是他的目的，C、D歪曲事实。

questions.q: What can we infer about Feynman from the story about the spinning plate?
options: He liked playing with plates more than doing serious research.
He solved the spinning plate problem and won a Nobel Prize.
His curiosity about a trivial event contributed to his later work.
He was criticized for wasting time during lunch.
questions.explain: 费曼对旋转餐盘的好奇引导他思考旋转粒子的数学，后来与量子电动力学相关，因此C（推断）正确。A是表面误解，B中诺奖不是因此问题直接获得，D无依据。

questions.q: The word 'controversy' in Paragraph 8 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: controversy意为“争议”，指公众的争论或分歧，因此B正确。
